sections.h2: Which offices touch a Woodbridge property tax bill?
sections.html:
A Woodbridge bill passes through three public desks. The township Tax Assessor puts a value on each parcel, the Tax Collection Office sends the bill and takes the money, and the Middlesex County Board of Taxation rules when an owner disputes the value. Middlesex County says on its own page that property tax is collected by the municipality, and the county then receives its share.

Where Woodbridge owners go for each property tax task, per the township Assessor and Tax Collector pages and the county Tax Board page
OfficeHandlesAddress, phone, hours
Township Tax AssessorValuing every parcel, new construction included, and running tax appeals on the township sideMunicipal Building, 1 Main Street, Woodbridge 07095; 732-602-6002
Tax Collection OfficeProperty tax and water or sewer bills and paymentsTown Hall, 1 Main Street, first floor; weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Tuesdays to 6:30 p.m.
Middlesex County Tax BoardCertifying assessments and deciding appeals75 Bayard Street, 4th floor, New Brunswick 08901; 732-745-3350; weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:15 p.m.

State law requires the assessor to hold a state certification (N.J.S.A. 54:1-35.25). The Tax Board looks after 25 municipalities across Middlesex County.

sections.h2: What is the Woodbridge billing calendar?
sections.html:
Four installments fall on the first of February, May, August and November. Bills arrive by mail in January and again in July.

Sewer runs on its own track. One notice posted for the second-half sewer bill named October 1 as the due date and Friday, October 10 as the final day before penalty, and it added that the date of receipt counts, not the postmark. Check the stub on your own bill for the dates that apply to you.

Closing close to a due date? Phone the Tax Collection Office and ask how it treats a payment that arrives a few days late before you count on any grace.

sections.h2: What are the ways to pay Woodbridge taxes?
sections.html:
The township offers five channels, each with its own cost.

  • Online, through the Taxpayer Information site. Search for your property, choose Make Payment, and follow the prompts. Electronic checks add $1.95, and cards add roughly 2.95 percent.
  • At the Town Hall counter, first floor, with cash, check or money order.
  • In the drop-off box outside Town Hall.
  • By check payable to Township of Woodbridge, mailed to P.O. Box 5004, Woodbridge, NJ 07095.
  • Through ACH direct withdrawal, using separate forms for tax and sewer.

The counter stays open until 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Sellers settling a balance right before the deed goes out will find online payment or a certified check at the counter the quickest.

sections.h2: What is the route for contesting a Woodbridge assessment?
sections.html:
A petition goes to the Middlesex County Board of Taxation. It can be filed online through the my.njappeal.com portal after you set up an account, and you can upload exhibits at filing or up to seven calendar days ahead of the hearing, by 4:00 p.m.

For added or omitted assessments the Board's cutoff is December 1 at 4:15 p.m., and the paper must be in the office, not just postmarked. A December 1 that falls on a weekend or holiday slides to the next business day. When an appraisal serves as evidence in those cases, the appraiser must show up and testify.

Owners turned down for the senior or disabled deduction have a separate route: Form A-1, filed with the county board by April 1 after the denial. For a regular assessment appeal, call the Tax Board at 732-745-3350 to confirm the deadline tied to your notice.

sections.h2: Which Woodbridge tax breaks should an owner check?
sections.html:
New Jersey takes $250 a year off the tax bill of qualifying owners who are 65 or older or disabled and have lived in the state at least a year. You need to own and occupy the house on October 1 of the pretax year, apply on time, and stay under the state's income cap.

  • Submit Form PTD with your proofs to the township assessor or collector.
  • Renew with Form PD5 by March 1 every year.
  • A surviving spouse or civil union partner aged 55 or more can carry the deduction on the same home.
  • A veteran deduction form is posted on the township Tax Collector page.

The state Division of Taxation held a Property Tax Relief filing event on November 2, 2026, at its Trenton office, with four regional offices staying open to 8:00 p.m. That evening has passed, so ask the Division or the township about the next filing window.

sections.h2: How should a Woodbridge seller handle unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Get a written balance for your block and lot from the Tax Collection Office before the contract is signed. With quarterly billing, a closing in the middle of a quarter can leave part of a period to settle, so ask how a late payment is credited.

Put the receipts for recent quarters in the closing folder. A separate sewer balance needs its own figure, because sewer follows a different calendar, and the buyer's closing agent will want both numbers.

If the assessed value looks wrong, take that up with the Assessor at 732-602-6002 before listing the house.

sections.h2: What should owners know about the Woodbridge area itself?
sections.html:
Woodbridge was chartered by Charles II on June 1, 1669, and ranks as the oldest original township in New Jersey. At 24.61 square miles in northern Middlesex County, it held 103,639 people in 2020, the seventh-largest count among the state's municipalities. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 104,802.

No incorporated towns sit inside it. Instead it is a set of communities: Avenel, Colonia, Fords, Hopelawn, Iselin, Keasbey, Menlo Park Terrace, Port Reading, Sewaren and Woodbridge proper, each with its own ZIP code or census place. A mayor and a nine-member council run the government under the Faulkner Act.

Transportation is the area's calling card. Turnpike Exit 11 leads into the township, the Garden State Parkway passes exits 127 through 132, and U.S. 1 and 9 share a corridor with Routes 27, 35, 184 and 440. NJ Transit stops at Metropark, Avenel and Woodbridge stations, and Metropark adds Amtrak. Woodbridge Center is the fourth-largest mall in New Jersey, and Wakefern Food Corporation, owner of ShopRite, has headquarters in Keasbey.

Water shapes many lots. Nearly one fifth of the land is inside FEMA flood hazard areas, with repeated tidal flooding along the Woodbridge River, the Raritan at Keasbey and the Arthur Kill at Sewaren and Port Reading. Schools belong to the Woodbridge Township School District, which operated 25 schools for 13,836 students in 2022 to 2023.

In Census estimates for 2020 to 2024, an owned home has a median value of $433,000, and renters pay a median $1,959 in gross rent. Households number 36,781 at 2.75 people each, and 40.6 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree. Two of every three homes are owner occupied, median household income is $108,928, and the average commute takes 32.5 minutes.

sections.h2: How big are the Woodbridge communities, and what green space do they share?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted these places inside the township: Iselin 20,088, Woodbridge proper 19,839, Colonia 18,609, Avenel 16,290, Fords 12,941, Port Reading 3,921, Keasbey 3,027, Sewaren 2,885, Menlo Park Terrace 2,806 and Hopelawn 2,603. Which one your house sits in affects the school routes, the train station and the flood exposure a buyer will ask about.

Woodbridge keeps a lot of open ground for a place this dense. Merrill Park covers 179 acres along the South Branch Rahway River, the Oros Wildlife Preserve holds 67 acres on the Woodbridge River, and Heards Brook Park sits in the middle of Woodbridge proper. The Middlesex Greenway is a 3.5-mile rail trail from Metuchen to Woodbridge that forms part of the East Coast Greenway.

The township maintains 244.16 of its 303.32 miles of roads. The county looks after 28.79 miles, the state 17.69 and the Turnpike Authority 12.68, based on the 2010 road survey cited for the township.

faqs.q: What are the Woodbridge property tax due dates?
faqs.a: Installments are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with bills mailed in January and July.

faqs.q: Where can I pay a Woodbridge tax bill in person?
faqs.a: Use the Tax Collection Office on the first floor of Town Hall. Cash, checks and money orders are accepted, and the counter runs late on Tuesdays.

faqs.q: Does Woodbridge charge a fee to pay taxes online?
faqs.a: Yes. An electronic check costs $1.95, and a credit or debit card costs about 2.95 percent of the payment.

faqs.q: Who hears a Woodbridge property tax appeal?
faqs.a: The Middlesex County Board of Taxation hears it. You can file through the Board's online portal or call 732-745-3350 for help.

faqs.q: Is there a senior property tax deduction in Woodbridge?
faqs.a: Yes, a $250 annual deduction for owners 65 or older or disabled who meet New Jersey's residency and income rules. Apply on Form PTD, and renew it each March 1 with Form PD5.
